newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait finance minister survives MPs' grilling.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait finance minister survives MPs' grilling.

text.p: Kuwait's parliament on Tuesday closed a stormy debate on alleged corruption in state institutions without calling for a no-confidence vote on the country's finance minister.
In a clear victory for the government and deputy prime minister and finance minister Nasser al-Rodhan, 31 of 52 MPs present voted to close the debate.

A no-confidence motion, which would have required the support of only 10 MPs, was not presented at the end of da y-long debate, apparently because Rodhan's opponents did not muster the required support, parliament sources said.
Support for the motion by 24 of 46 elected MPs would have forced Rodhan to resign.

"We are talking about the supervision role and preventing the crime before it happens," said Mishari al-Osaimi, one of three opposition MPs who presented the request to grill Rodhan over alleged violations by institutions he heads.
"We shall continue the attack," Osaimi vowed.

Rodhan was first made finance minister in 1991 shortly after the Gulf War over Iraq's occupation of Kuwait. He also chairs the Kuwait Investment Authority (KIA), which manages the state's foreign investments of more than $40 billion, the Central Bank and Kuwait Airways.
"We came here to reform...We did not come here to have a winner and a loser," liberal opposition MP Sami al-Munayes said.

Earlier in the day Munayes listed financial transactions which allegedly cost the state tens of millions of dollars. He claimed that corruption was rampant due to lack of measures to montior public funds and failure to conduct adequate checks when appointing officials in charge of state funds.
Rodhan responded by saying he was not the target of the questioning but it was aimed at bringing down the government.
He said the questioning document contained more than 50 accusations, using language "which should not be used in parliamentary work...Today we are before strange questioning.
"This is a good opportunity for me to prove that I entered the cabinet with a clean white robe which, with God's help, will always remain clean."
He then responded to each of the 10 issues presented in his questioning but Munayes said the answers were inadequate.

Rodhan's questioning, the 12th since Kuwait's first parliament in 1963, is the first of a cabinet minister by the parliament which was elected in October shortly prior to the appointment of the current cabinet.
